--- title: "[StepPca]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Project numeric columns onto their principal components. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_pca.py#L175-L362){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepPca( columns, *, num_comp=5, prefix="PC", keep_original_cols=False, role="predictor", id=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The selected numeric columns are replaced by ``num_comp`` principal-component columns ``{prefix}1 ... {prefix}{num_comp}``, or kept alongside them when ``keep_original_cols`` is ``True``. Each component is a linear combination of all the input columns, so no single component belongs to any one of them. Asking for more components than there are input columns yields fewer. The columns are centered but not scaled, so a column measured on a larger numeric range contributes more to the components; normalize first if that is not what you want. Rows with a missing value are excluded when the components are computed, and such a row gets ``NaN`` for every component. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [columns]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Selector]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Columns to project. Accepts a single column name, a list of names, a shoez selector such as ``Selectors.numeric_predictors()`` (see `Selectors` for the full set), or a narwhals or polars selector (``narwhals.selectors.numeric()``, ``polars.selectors.numeric()``). Selectors are resolved against the frame's schema when the recipe is fitted, so the same selector works on any backend. Only numeric columns are meaningful here. [num_comp]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[5]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of principal components to keep. Must be a positive integer. Default ``5``. [prefix]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["PC"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Prefix for the produced component column names. Default ``"PC"``. [keep_original_cols]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If ``True``, the source columns are kept alongside the components instead of being dropped. Default ``False``. [role]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["predictor"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Role assigned to the new component columns. Default ``"predictor"``. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"pca"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The two correlated columns are replaced by two principal components: ::: {#9fb2f3eb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame( {"x": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], "y": [2.1, 3.9, 6.1, 8.0]} ) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
x y
0 1.0 2.1
1 2.0 3.9
2 3.0 6.1
3 4.0 8.0
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#b8fe083b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepPca(s.numeric_predictors(), num_comp=2)) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_pca(select(role='predictor', type=NumericType)) [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` learns the component loadings: ::: {#cccc502b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 2 columns — 2 predictors Steps: step_pca(x, y → PC1, PC2) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` replaces the columns with their scores: ::: {#2046a5c7 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
PC1 PC2
0 -3.287069 0.028375
1 -1.229748 -0.057834
2 1.185062 0.035403
3 3.331755 -0.005944
``` ::: ::: ``num_comp`` caps how many components are kept: ::: {#4b9a368b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add(StepPca(s.numeric_predictors(), num_comp=1)) fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
PC1
0 -3.287069
1 -1.229748
2 1.185062
3 3.331755
``` ::: ::: ``keep_original_cols`` keeps the source columns alongside the components: ::: {#09e38a41 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add( StepPca(s.numeric_predictors(), num_comp=2, keep_original_cols=True) ) fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
x y PC1 PC2
0 1.0 2.1 -3.287069 0.028375
1 2.0 3.9 -1.229748 -0.057834
2 3.0 6.1 1.185062 0.035403
3 4.0 8.0 3.331755 -0.005944
``` ::: :::
